title: घान्द्रुक, सिक्लेस र ल्वाङमा पर्यटकको घुइँचो, बास पाउनै मुस्किल
content:
कास्की । तिहार र छठको बिदासँगै पर्यटकीय याम उत्कर्षमा पुगेपछि कास्कीका घान्द्रुक, सिक्लेस र ल्वाङ गाउँ पर्यटकले भरिभराउ भएका छन् । आन्तरिक पर्यटकको उल्लेख्य आगमनसँगै यी गाउँका होटल र घरबासमा पाहुनाको चाप बढेको छ । कतिपय पर्यटकले अग्रिम बुकिङ नगर्दा आवास पाउन कठिन भएको छ । न्नपूर्ण गाउँपालिका–१० र ११ मा पर्ने घान्द्रुकमा तिहारको भोलिपल्टदेखि पर्यटकको चहलपहल बढेको हो । घान्द्रुक पर्यटन व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष विक्रम गुरुङका अनुसार अहिले दैनिक तीन हजार चार सयदेखि तीन हजार पाँच सयसम्म पर्यटक गाउँ पुगिरहेका छन् । पर्यटकको चापले होटलमा कोठा पाउन कठिन भएपछि समितिले अग्रिम ‘बुकिङ’ गरेर मात्र भ्रमणमा आउन आग्रह गरेको छ । घान्द्रुक पुग्नेमा अधिकांश आन्तरिक पर्यटक छन् भने भारतीय तथा अन्य मुलुकका पर्यटकको आगमन पनि भइरहेको छ । अन्नपूर्ण चक्रीय पदमार्गको प्रमुख गन्तव्यका रूपमा रहेको घान्द्रुक अन्नपूर्ण आधार शिविर र पुनहिल–घोरेपानी पदमार्गमा पर्ने भएकाले पदयात्रीका लागि विश्रामस्थलसमेत हो । अन्नपूर्ण र माछापुच्छ्रे हिमशृङ्खलाको मनोरम दृश्य, गुरुङ समुदायको मौलिक संस्कृति, गाउँले परिवेश र स्थानीय आतिथ्य घान्द्रुकका मुख्य आकर्षण हुन् । सडक पहुँच विस्तार भएपछि पछिल्लो समय आन्तरिक पर्यटकको आगमन थप बढेको स्थानीय पर्यटन व्यवसायी बताउँछन् । पर्यटन व्यवस्थापन समितिका अनुसार गाउँमा रिसोर्टसहित ८० होटल र ३५ घरबास सञ्चालनमा छन् । मादी गाउँपालिका–१ स्थित सिक्लेस गाउँमा पनि पर्यटकको चाप उस्तै छ । पर्यटक सूचना केन्द्रका अनुसार तिहारको भोलिपल्ट एक हजार तीन सय २४ जना पर्यटक सिक्लेस पुगेका थिए । एकैपटक ठूलो सङ्ख्यामा पर्यटक आउँदा होटल व्यवस्थापनमा कठिनाइ भएको स्थानीय व्यवसायीले बताएका छन् । नमस्ते गेस्ट हाउसका सञ्चालक झरना गुरुङका अनुसार होटल आइतबारसम्मका लागि बुकिङ भइसकेको छ । नयाँ पाहुनालाई कोठा उपलब्ध गराउन कठिन भएपछि पर्यटकलाई होटलको अवस्था बुझेर अग्रिम बुकिङ गर्न आग्रह गरिएको उनले बताइन् । हिमालको काखमा अवस्थित सिक्लेस प्राकृतिक सौन्दर्यसँगै गुरुङ संस्कृति र परम्पराका लागि परिचित छ । एकै बान्कीका ढुङ्गा र जस्ताका छाना भएका घर, ढुङ्गे आँगन र बाटा, पुराना शैलीका झ्यालढोका तथा साँघुरा गल्लीले गाउँको मौलिक पहिचान झल्काउँछन् । मादी खोला, हरियाली वनपाखा र हिमाली दृश्यले जोकोही मन्त्रमुग्ध हुन्छन् । गुरुङ सङ्ग्रहालय, शान्ति स्मारक, सिक्लेस पार्क, मौलिक भेषभूषा, नाचगान र स्थानीय परिकार यहाँका थप आकर्षण हुन् । सिक्लेस–कपुचे–कोरी पदमार्ग सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पदयात्राका लागि आउने पर्यटकको सङ्ख्या पनि बढेको स्थानीय व्यवसायी बताउँछन् । दुई दशकअघि सामुदायिक घरबासबाट सुरु भएको यहाँको पर्यटन व्यवसाय अहिले होटल र घरबाससम्म विस्तार भएको छ । पोखरा महानगरपालिकासँग जोडिएको माछापुच्छ्रे गाउँपालिका–८ को ल्वाङ गाउँमा पनि पर्यटकको आगमन बढेको छ । तिहारको भोलिपल्टदेखि होटल र घरबासमा पाहुना भरिएपछि व्यवस्थापनमा कठिनाइ भएको ल्वाङ सामुदायिक घरबास व्यवस्थापन समितिका निवर्तमान अध्यक्ष मञ्जु गुरुङले बताइन् । विसं २०६७ मा सात घरबाट सुरु भएको ल्वाङको घरबास व्यवसाय अहिले २६ घरमा विस्तार भएको छ । यहाँका घरबासमा एकै रातमा ४ सय सम्म पाहुनालाई आवासको व्यवस्था गर्ने क्षमता छ । प्रकृति र गुरुङ संस्कृतिको अनुभव लिन चाहने पर्यटकका लागि ल्वाङ लोकप्रिय गन्तव्य बन्दै गएको छ । समुद्र सतहबाट एक हजार ४ सय मिटर उचाइमा रहेको ल्वाङबाट माछापुच्छ्रे र अन्नपूर्ण हिमशृङ्खलामा देखिने सूर्योदयको दृश्य आकर्षक मानिन्छ । गाउँको सिरानमा एक हजार २ सय रोपनी क्षेत्रफलमा फैलिएको चियाबारी यहाँको अर्को प्रमुख आकर्षण हो । चियाबारी, गुरुङ संस्कार, रैथाने खाना र स्थानीय जीवनशैलीको अनुभव लिन स्वदेशी तथा विदेशी पर्यटक गाउँ पुग्ने गरेका छन् । ल्वाङमा पर्यटकले स्थानीय परिकार बनाउने तरिका, खेतीपाती र निगालोबाट डोको तथा सेखुजस्ता सामग्री बनाउने सीपबारे जानकारी लिन पाउँछन् । अन्नपूर्ण आधार शिविर र मर्दी पदमार्ग जाने पर्यटकले पनि यहाँ विश्राम गर्ने गरेका छन् । नजिकैको पोखरा क्यानोनिङ र घलेल गाउँले यस क्षेत्रको पर्यटकीय आकर्षण थपेका छन् । पोखराबाट घान्द्रुक, सिक्लेस र ल्वाङसम्म सडकबाट पुग्न सकिने भएकाले यी गाउँको भ्रमण सहज बनेको छ । प्राकृतिक सौन्दर्य, मौलिक संस्कृति, पदयात्रा र घरबासको अनुभवले यी गन्तव्य पर्यटकको रोजाइमा पर्दै आएका छन् । तिहार र छठको बिदासँगै बढेको पर्यटक आगमनले स्थानीय पर्यटन व्यवसायलाई चलायमान बनाएको छ भने पर्यटकको चाप व्यवस्थापन र पर्याप्त आवासको उपलब्धता चुनौतीका रूपमा देखिएको छ । Kaski. With the peak of the tourist season with the Tihar and Chhath holidays, the villages of Ghandruk, Sikles and Lwang in Kaski have become crowded with tourists. With the significant influx of domestic tourists, the pressure of guests in hotels and homes in these villages has increased. It has been difficult for some tourists to find accommodation as they do not book in advance. Tourist activity has increased in Ghandruk, located in Nnapurna Rural Municipality-10 and 11, since the day after Tihar. According to Bikram Gurung, Chairman of the Ghandruk Tourism Management Committee, 3,400 to 3,500 tourists are currently visiting the village daily. As the influx of tourists makes it difficult to find rooms in hotels, the committee has urged people to book in advance. Most of the tourists who reach Ghandruk are domestic tourists, but tourists from India and other countries are also arriving. Ghandruk, which is a major destination on the Annapurna Circuit Trek, is also a resting place for trekkers as it falls on the Annapurna Base Camp and Punhill-Ghorepani Trek. The scenic views of the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre mountain ranges, the original culture of the Gurung community, the rural environment and local hospitality are the main attractions of Ghandruk. Local tourism entrepreneurs say that the arrival of domestic tourists has increased recently after the expansion of road access. According to the Tourism Management Committee, there are 80 hotels, including resorts, and 35 homestays in operation in the village. The tourist pressure is also similar in Sikles village located in Madi Rural Municipality-1. According to the Tourist Information Center, 1,324 tourists had reached Sikles the day after Tihar. Local businessmen have said that the large number of tourists arriving at once has created difficulties in hotel management. According to Jharana Gurung, the owner of Namaste Guest House, the hotel is fully booked until Sunday. She said that tourists are being urged to book in advance after understanding the hotel's condition as it is difficult to provide rooms to new guests. Nestled in the lap of the Himalayas, Sikles is known for its natural beauty as well as Gurung culture and tradition. The houses with the same pattern of stone and zinc roofs, stone courtyards and paths, old-style windows and doors, and narrow streets reflect the original identity of the village. The Madi River, the lush greenery, and the mountainous views enchant anyone. Gurung Museum, Peace Monument, Sikles Park, original costumes, dances and songs and local dishes are some of the additional attractions here. Local businessmen say that the number of tourists coming for trekking has also increased after the Sikles-Kapuche-Kori trekking route came into operation. The tourism business here, which started with community houses two decades ago, has now expanded to hotels and homes. The arrival of tourists has also increased in Lwang village of Machhapuchhre Rural Municipality-8, which is connected to Pokhara Metropolitan City. Manju Gurung, the outgoing chairperson of the Lwang Community Housing Management Committee, said that management has become difficult after hotels and homes have been filled with guests since the day after Tihar. The homestay business in Lwang, which started with seven houses in 2067 BS, has now expanded to 26 houses. The homes here have the capacity to accommodate up to 400 guests in a single night. Lwang is becoming a popular destination for tourists who want to experience nature and Gurung culture. The view of sunrise over Machhapuchhre and Annapurna ranges from Lwang, which is located at an altitude of 1,400 meters above sea level, is considered attractive. Another major attraction here is the tea plantation spread over an area of 1,200 ropanis at the top of the village. Domestic and foreign tourists visit the village to experience the tea plantation, Gurung culture, traditional food, and local lifestyle. In Lwang, tourists can learn about local cuisine, farming, and the skills of making materials like doko and sekhu from straw. Tourists going to Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Trek also rest here. Nearby Pokhara Canyoning and Ghalel Village have added to the tourist attraction of this area. Ghandruk, Sikles and Lwang are easily accessible by road from Pokhara, making it easy to visit these villages. These destinations have become popular among tourists due to their natural beauty, unique culture, trekking and homestay experience. The increased tourist arrivals during the Tihar and Chhath holidays have boosted the local tourism industry, while managing the tourist pressure and providing adequate accommodation are seen as challenges.

गुरुङले बताइन् । विसं २०६७ मा सात घरबाट सुरु भएको ल्वाङको घरबास व्यवसाय अहिले २६ घरमा विस्तार भएको छ । यहाँका घरबासमा एकै रातमा ४ सय सम्म पाहुनालाई आवासको व्यवस्था गर्ने क्षमता छ । प्रकृति र गुरुङ संस्कृतिको अनुभव लिन चाहने पर्यटकका लागि ल्वाङ लोकप्रिय गन्तव्य बन्दै गएको छ । समुद्र सतहबाट एक हजार ४ सय मिटर उचाइमा रहेको ल्वाङबाट माछापुच्छ्रे र अन्नपूर्ण हिमशृङ्खलामा देखिने सूर्योदयको दृश्य आकर्षक मानिन्छ । गाउँको सिरानमा एक हजार २ सय रोपनी क्षेत्रफलमा फैलिएको चियाबारी यहाँको अर्को प्रमुख आकर्षण हो । चियाबारी, गुरुङ संस्कार, रैथाने खाना र स्थानीय जीवनशैलीको अनुभव लिन स्वदेशी तथा विदेशी पर्यटक गाउँ पुग्ने गरेका छन् । ल्वाङमा पर्यटकले स्थानीय परिकार बनाउने तरिका, खेतीपाती र निगालोबाट डोको तथा सेखुजस्ता सामग्री बनाउने सीपबारे जानकारी लिन पाउँछन् । अन्नपूर्ण आधार शिविर र मर्दी पदमार्ग जाने पर्यटकले पनि यहाँ विश्राम गर्ने गरेका छन् । नजिकैको पोखरा क्यानोनिङ र घलेल गाउँले यस क्षेत्रको पर्यटकीय आकर्षण थपेका छन् । पोखराबाट घान्द्रुक, सिक्लेस र ल्वाङसम्म सडकबाट पुग्न सकिने भएकाले यी गाउँको भ्रमण सहज बनेको छ । प्राकृतिक सौन्दर्य, मौलिक संस्कृति, पदयात्रा र घरबासको अनुभवले यी गन्तव्य पर्यटकको रोजाइमा पर्दै आएका छन् । तिहार र छठको बिदासँगै बढेको पर्यटक आगमनले स्थानीय पर्यटन व्यवसायलाई चलायमान बनाएको छ भने पर्यटकको चाप व्यवस्थापन र पर्याप्त आवासको उपलब्धता चुनौतीका रूपमा देखिएको छ ।

कास्की । तिहार र छठको बिदासँगै पर्यटकीय याम उत्कर्षमा पुगेपछि कास्कीका घान्द्रुक, सिक्लेस र ल्वाङ गाउँ पर्यटकले भरिभराउ भएका छन् । आन्तरिक पर्यटकको उल्लेख्य आगमनसँगै यी गाउँका होटल र घरबासमा पाहुनाको चाप बढेको छ । कतिपय पर्यटकले अग्रिम बुकिङ नगर्दा आवास पाउन कठिन भएको छ ।

न्नपूर्ण गाउँपालिका–१० र ११ मा पर्ने घान्द्रुकमा तिहारको भोलिपल्टदेखि पर्यटकको चहलपहल बढेको हो । घान्द्रुक पर्यटन व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष विक्रम गुरुङका अनुसार अहिले दैनिक तीन हजार चार सयदेखि तीन हजार पाँच सयसम्म पर्यटक गाउँ पुगिरहेका छन् । पर्यटकको चापले होटलमा कोठा पाउन कठिन भएपछि समितिले अग्रिम ‘बुकिङ’ गरेर मात्र भ्रमणमा आउन आग्रह गरेको छ ।

घान्द्रुक पुग्नेमा अधिकांश आन्तरिक पर्यटक छन् भने भारतीय तथा अन्य मुलुकका पर्यटकको आगमन पनि भइरहेको छ । अन्नपूर्ण चक्रीय पदमार्गको प्रमुख गन्तव्यका रूपमा रहेको घान्द्रुक अन्नपूर्ण आधार शिविर र पुनहिल–घोरेपानी पदमार्गमा पर्ने भएकाले पदयात्रीका लागि विश्रामस्थलसमेत हो ।

मादी गाउँपालिका–१ स्थित सिक्लेस गाउँमा पनि पर्यटकको चाप उस्तै छ । पर्यटक सूचना केन्द्रका अनुसार तिहारको भोलिपल्ट एक हजार तीन सय २४ जना पर्यटक सिक्लेस पुगेका थिए । एकैपटक ठूलो सङ्ख्यामा पर्यटक आउँदा होटल व्यवस्थापनमा कठिनाइ भएको स्थानीय व्यवसायीले बताएका छन् ।

नमस्ते गेस्ट हाउसका सञ्चालक झरना गुरुङका अनुसार होटल आइतबारसम्मका लागि बुकिङ भइसकेको छ । नयाँ पाहुनालाई कोठा उपलब्ध गराउन कठिन भएपछि पर्यटकलाई होटलको अवस्था बुझेर अग्रिम बुकिङ गर्न आग्रह गरिएको उनले बताइन् ।

हिमालको काखमा अवस्थित सिक्लेस प्राकृतिक सौन्दर्यसँगै गुरुङ संस्कृति र परम्पराका लागि परिचित छ । एकै बान्कीका ढुङ्गा र जस्ताका छाना भएका घर, ढुङ्गे आँगन र बाटा, पुराना शैलीका झ्यालढोका तथा साँघुरा गल्लीले गाउँको मौलिक पहिचान झल्काउँछन् । मादी खोला, हरियाली वनपाखा र हिमाली दृश्यले जोकोही मन्त्रमुग्ध हुन्छन् ।

गुरुङ सङ्ग्रहालय, शान्ति स्मारक, सिक्लेस पार्क, मौलिक भेषभूषा, नाचगान र स्थानीय परिकार यहाँका थप आकर्षण हुन् । सिक्लेस–कपुचे–कोरी पदमार्ग सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पदयात्राका लागि आउने पर्यटकको सङ्ख्या पनि बढेको स्थानीय व्यवसायी बताउँछन् । दुई दशकअघि सामुदायिक घरबासबाट सुरु भएको यहाँको पर्यटन व्यवसाय अहिले होटल र घरबाससम्म विस्तार भएको छ ।

Kaski. With the peak of the tourist season with the Tihar and Chhath holidays, the villages of Ghandruk, Sikles and Lwang in Kaski have become crowded with tourists. With the significant influx of domestic tourists, the pressure of guests in hotels and homes in these villages has increased. It has been difficult for some tourists to find accommodation as they do not book in advance. Tourist activity has increased in Ghandruk, located in Nnapurna Rural Municipality-10 and 11, since the day after Tihar. According to Bikram Gurung, Chairman of the Ghandruk Tourism Management Committee, 3,400 to 3,500 tourists are currently visiting the village daily. As the influx of tourists makes it difficult to find rooms in hotels, the committee has urged people to book in advance. Most of the tourists who reach Ghandruk are domestic tourists, but tourists from India and other countries are also arriving. Ghandruk, which is a major destination on the Annapurna Circuit Trek, is also a resting place for trekkers as it falls on the Annapurna Base Camp and Punhill-Ghorepani Trek. The scenic views of the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre mountain ranges, the original culture of the Gurung community, the rural environment and local hospitality are the main attractions of Ghandruk. Local tourism entrepreneurs say that the arrival of domestic tourists has increased recently after the expansion of road access. According to the Tourism Management Committee, there are 80 hotels, including resorts, and 35 homestays in operation in the village. The tourist pressure is also similar in Sikles village located in Madi Rural Municipality-1. According to the Tourist Information Center, 1,324 tourists had reached Sikles the day after Tihar. Local businessmen have said that the large number of tourists arriving at once has created difficulties in hotel management. According to Jharana Gurung, the owner of Namaste Guest House, the hotel is fully booked until Sunday. She said that tourists are being urged to book in advance after understanding the hotel's condition as it is difficult to provide rooms to new guests. Nestled in the lap of the Himalayas, Sikles is known for its natural beauty as well as Gurung culture and tradition. The houses with the same pattern of stone and zinc roofs, stone courtyards and paths, old-style windows and doors, and narrow streets reflect the original identity of the village. The Madi River, the lush greenery, and the mountainous views enchant anyone. Gurung Museum, Peace Monument, Sikles Park, original costumes, dances and songs and local dishes are some of the additional attractions here. Local businessmen say that the number of tourists coming for trekking has also increased after the Sikles-Kapuche-Kori trekking route came into operation. The tourism business here, which started with community houses two decades ago, has now expanded to hotels and homes. The arrival of tourists has also increased in Lwang village of Machhapuchhre Rural Municipality-8, which is connected to Pokhara Metropolitan City. Manju Gurung, the outgoing chairperson of the Lwang Community Housing Management Committee, said that management has become difficult after hotels and homes have been filled with guests since the day after Tihar. The homestay business in Lwang, which started with seven houses in 2067 BS, has now expanded to 26 houses. The homes here have the capacity to accommodate up to 400 guests in a single night. Lwang is becoming a popular destination for tourists who want to experience nature and Gurung culture. The view of sunrise over Machhapuchhre and Annapurna ranges from Lwang, which is located at an altitude of 1,400 meters above sea level, is considered attractive. Another major attraction here is the tea plantation spread over an area of 1,200 ropanis at the top of the village. Domestic and foreign tourists visit the village to experience the tea plantation, Gurung culture, traditional food, and local lifestyle. In Lwang, tourists can learn about local cuisine, farming, and the skills of making materials like doko and sekhu from straw. Tourists going to Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Trek also rest here. Nearby Pokhara Canyoning and Ghalel Village have added to the tourist attraction of this area. Ghandruk, Sikles and Lwang are easily accessible by road from Pokhara, making it easy to visit these villages. These destinations have become popular among tourists due to their natural beauty, unique culture, trekking and homestay experience. The increased tourist arrivals during the Tihar and Chhath holidays have boosted the local tourism industry, while managing the tourist pressure and providing adequate accommodation are seen as challenges.
